How to prepare a photography brief

A useful starting point for aligning the story, shot list and delivery requirements before a shoot.

Charlot Crea31 October 20262 min readSample article
In this articleStart with the purposeBuild a focused shot listExplain where the images will appearLeave room for the conversation

Start with the purpose

A photography brief should explain what the images need to communicate. Introduce the brand, the subject and the audience. A campaign aimed at potential guests may need a different visual rhythm from an architecture portfolio. Describe the feeling you want the collection to create, then connect that ambition to a practical use.

Build a focused shot list

Group the requested photographs by subject or space. Separate essential frames from optional ideas, and note access restrictions or details that need preparation. References are useful when you explain what you like about them: light, colour, composition or atmosphere. They should support a conversation rather than become a list of images to copy.

Explain where the images will appear

List the intended channels, such as a website, printed brochure or social campaign. Mention horizontal and vertical requirements, approximate delivery needs and any existing brand guidelines. Usage rights and delivery formats should be discussed as part of the project scope.

Leave room for the conversation

Include the location, preferred dates, point of contact and any important deadlines. A first brief does not need every production detail. Its purpose is to reveal priorities and open questions early, so the team can build a realistic approach together.
